decisions.language: PoC1: Swift 6, compiler observed 6.3.2. PoC2 macOS: Swift/AppKit adapter around a language-neutral canonical theme contract. Rust remains a candidate for the portable core and renderer; no production language is frozen. Node.js is governance tooling only.
decisions.runtime: PoC1 frozen as evidence. PoC2 targets a native macOS connector app plus a separate wallpaper adapter, deployment target macOS 14 and qualification limited to MAC-01 macOS 26.2. Windows, Wayland, GNOME and X11 require distinct connectors behind the same product contract.
decisions.frontend: PoC2 uses one authoritative control surface at a time. Native connector UI owns permissions and recovery; the portable theme owns fully stylable semantic menus, buttons, panels, system_controls and 2D/3D scene presentation. PoC2 diagnostics are not product design.
decisions.backend: PoC2 has no server, PTY, game reader or LLM runtime. App and wallpaper communicate through a bounded typed connector protocol; XPC versus App Group transport remains an experiment.
decisions.storage: PoC2 has one canonical JSON theme fixture, minimal connector preferences and reconstructible artifacts under ignored dist/. No ROM, terminal content or private filenames are stored.
decisions.deployment: PoC2: local stable bundle identities, explicit install/activation and documented rollback; no autostart or product installer yet. The private Apple wallpaper provider path remains experimental and is not an App Store claim.
decisions.observability: PoC2: bounded capability, lifecycle, command/receipt and render counters without terminal content, filenames or desktop capture; every proof is dated and tied to MAC-01.
decisions.security: PoC2 defaults to passive input. Global click handling is enabled only with TCC permission and positive Finder-background classification; unknown targets fail open to macOS. No shell, network, ROM, IA or converter is in scope.
decisions.performance: PoC2 uses event invalidation, no timer for static scenes, and measured incremental energy against the native desktop across all related processes; no numerical budget is claimed before the benchmark.
